newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon banks to cut prime lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon banks to cut prime lending rate.

text.p: The Lebanese Banks Association said on Thursday it had cut the Lebanese pound prime lending rate to 18 percent from 24 percent following cuts in T-bill rates.

The association which groups 79 of Lebanon's 82 banks said in a statement that the rate cut was decided at a meeting of its board on Tuesday. The last rate cut was in January 1996, when the prime rate was cut to 24 percent from 30 percent.

Makram Sader, secretary-general of the banks association, said the cut was in line with a declining Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bill yields and also aimed at boosting lending in the local currency.

"There are two reasons behind cutting the prime rate. The first is the trend of falling treasury bill rates and the second is boosting lending in Lebanese pounds, which is very important," Sader told Reuters.
Lebanese T-bills of three-month, six-month, one-year and two-year maturities currently yield 14.21 percent, 16.01 percent, 16.76 percent and 18.70 percent respectively.
They were 14.61 percent, 16.92 percent, 17.78 percent and 21.62 percent three months ago.
The banks association also urged commercial banks to lower the pound credit rate for three-month, six-month, one-year and two-year time deposits to less than the corresponding T-bill yields.
The association said the dollar prime rate for Lebanon's major commercial banks was still 10.5 percent.
